row.team_price_text: Pay-as-you-go AWS usage; IAM Identity Center no extra charge
row.evidence: AWS's IAM Identity Center FAQ says "IAM Identity Center is offered at no extra charge", and the user guide says it supports automatic provisioning of users and groups from your IdP using SCIM v2.0.
row.notes: New row. AWS is usage-priced; workforce SSO and SCIM for AWS accounts and apps run through IAM Identity Center, which has no extra charge, so status is free and per-user team fields stay null. Classic IAM users have no SCIM. SCIM is a subset: bearer token valid one year, no /Bulk, /Me or /Search, eq-only filters, single-valued multi-value attributes, group members not returned on read. Once SCIM is on, users can't be added or edited in the console. Identity Store API (create/update/delete users, groups, memberships) stays available alongside SCIM. Google Workspace SCIM covers users only (no group push). IAM Identity Center also acts as an IdP for AWS-managed and customer SAML apps but does not push SCIM outbound.

plans.name: IAM Identity Center
plans.notes: AWS services are usage-priced; IAM Identity Center itself carries no charge.

auth.token_source: IAM Identity Center console > Settings > Identity source > Actions > Manage provisioning > Access tokens > Generate token

deprovision.data_retained: Behaviour depends on the IdP: Okta unassignment disables the user; DELETE removes the user permanently. Disabled or deleted users can't sign in or create new sessions, but existing IAM role sessions in the console/CLI are not ended by ending Identity Center sessions.
deprovision.notes: No per-seat charge, so seat freeing does not apply.

core: addresses (single value: formatted, streetAddress, locality, region, postalCode, country)
group: members (value, type, $ref; not returned on read)

roles.how: SCIM roles attribute (single value only); AWS access itself is granted through permission-set assignments to users or groups, not via SCIM.

rate_limits.text: 25 TPS per write API and 40 TPS per read API, per Identity Store instance; increases via support case.

limitations.text: Only eq filters (with and); no /Me, /Bulk or /Search endpoints.
Multi-valued user attributes are not supported; only single values.
GetGroup/ListGroups return an empty members list; PatchGroup doesn't support remove-all or replace.
After SCIM is enabled, users cannot be added or edited in the console.
Google Workspace SCIM provisions users only; groups must be created manually or via the Identity Store API.
SCIM tokens expire after one year and must be rotated or sync stops.

auth.notes: AWS JSON protocol with IAM permissions; callable by principals in the management or delegated administrator account. Scopes listed are IAM action names (the docs show identitystore:Create*/Update*/Delete* in an SCP example).

endpoints.purpose: Add a member to a group

webhooks_user_events.notes: Changes are logged as CloudTrail events, which can feed EventBridge; no dedicated user webhooks documented here.

audit_log_api.notes: Via AWS CloudTrail (SCIM and Identity Store calls logged as events).

rate_limits.text: Identity Store APIs: 20 TPS per API per Identity Store instance.

okta.notes: OIN markup: SAML, SCIM, Create, Update, Deactivate, Group Push, Group Linking, Schema Discovery checked.

google.notes: From AWS's Google Workspace tutorial; user provisioning only, no group push. Google's own catalogue page not loaded.

onelogin.notes: From AWS's OneLogin guide; OneLogin catalogue not loaded.

jumpcloud.notes: From AWS's JumpCloud guide; jumpcloud.com blocks plain requests.

fallbacks.other_sync: Manual provisioning in the console when the IdP lacks SCIM; Active Directory via AWS Directory Service as identity source

open_questions: Whether SCIM PATCH active=false and Okta deactivation are reversible (reactivate) is not explicitly documented.
Custom SCIM attributes/extensions beyond the enterprise schema are not documented.
Whether IAM Identity Center creates users just-in-time on SAML sign-in is not documented; the docs say users must be provisioned by SCIM or manually.
